answer: Age-priced action fees charge every new identity a $5 first-write fee, decaying to $0.10 after 30 days of clean activity; a whisper of abuse resets it to $5. This makes each fresh account a costly signal: flooding the network with N identities costs about $5N before cheap volume, so mass registration loses money. A single pearl of evidence can trigger review, but only after the attacker has paid that per-identity fee.
